newsitem.title: UK: UK approves new Procter & Gamble bone disease drug.
newsitem.headline: UK approves new Procter & Gamble bone disease drug.

text.p: Britain's Medicines Control Agency on Wednesday licensed the Procter & Gamble drug, Didronel PMO, for the prevention of the bone thinning disease, osteoporosis, the Department of Health said on Thursday.

Didronel has been available in the U.K. since 1992 for the treatment of established spinal osteoporosis. The new license will make it possible for the drug, known generically as Cyclical Etidronate, to be used as an alternative to hormone replacement therapy for post-menopausal women.

The ruling also clears the drug for use in the prevention and treatment of corticosteroid induced osteoporosis. Corticosteroids are widely used in the treatment of asthma and rheumatoid arthritis. But they can cause bone loss and may result in fractures.

"Steroids are important, but they can cause complications with the skeleton," Dr Roger Francis told a news conference. Francis is senior lecturer in medicine at the Freeman Hospital, Newcastle upon Tyne in north-east England.

Osteoporosis leads to an estimated 60,000 hip, 50,000 wrist and 40,000 spinal fractures in the U.K. each year. An estimated one in three women and one in 12 men are considered at risk of acquiring the bone disease.

Britain's National Health Service spends an estimated 750 million pounds ($1.2 billion) per year in treating bone fractures. "If we could save this sum, there could be a huge benefit to the health service," said Linda Edwards, director of the National Osteoporosis Society.
The cost of treating one patient with Didronel for a year is 160 pounds. The drug is considered safe and effective for use for up to seven years, Francis said.

For post-menopausal women, the preferred treatment for osteoporosis still is hormone replacement therapy. However, not all women either want or can receive the oestrogen treatment. Women at risk from hormone replacement therapy for example would be those with a previous history of breast cancer. For this group and for women who give up hormone replacement therapy, Didronel is a very welcome alternative, Edwards said.

Didronel has been approved for the treatment of osteoporosis in Canada and several other European countries, in addition to the U.K. Procter & Gamble is seeking approval to sell the drug for prevention of the bone disease elsewhere in Europe and in Canada.
The U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved Didronel for the treatment Paget's disease, another bone disease. But the FDA hasn't approved the drug for osteoporosis.
Merck & Co.'s Fosamax is a major rival to Didronel.
